Rainfall detection

Source: R/rainfallDetection.R
rainfallDetection.Rd

Detects rainfall in a Wave. The "bedoya2017" method follows (Bedoya et al. 2017) : the mean power spectral density of the 600-1200 Hz band, where rain falling on vegetation is loudest, together with the ratio of that mean to its standard deviation across the band, both of which must clear a threshold. One band is what the paper specifies; the two bands of the hardRain package are that package's own addition rather than part of the method cited here.

Usage

rainfallDetection(wave, method = "bedoya2017", ...)

Arguments

wave

A Wave object to detect rainfall in. Stereo Wave and WaveMC objects are passed to allChannels(), which returns one value per channel.

method

Which rainfall detection method to use ("bedoya2017")

...

Other arguments to pass to rain detection function

Value

Numeric value from the rainfall detection algorithm chosen, or zero where the recording is not rainfall. For "bedoya2017" the value is the mean power spectral density of the 600-1200 Hz band in power per Hz, relative to the full scale of the format the wave is held in, so it is the same number whatever that bit depth is and is comparable between recordings. Its Tmean threshold is in those units. For multi-channel input, a list of such values.

Details

Two things here are not the paper's. Tsnr defaults to 3.5 where the paper reports 1.8, and the ratio is taken across the band's bins of a spectrum already averaged over the recording, which makes it rise with the recording's length: the same noise gives 4.0 over 0.05 s and 49 over 60 s. On labelled recordings that measure still separates rain (11 to 27) from everything else (1.4 to 5.8) far more cleanly than the alternatives, which is why it is kept, but Tsnr is a figure for a fixed clip length rather than an absolute one.

Tmean is in power per Hz relative to full scale and defaults to the paper's 0.9e-6, which is a calibration rather than a constant: the level of a band depends on recorder gain, and across ten labelled rain recordings from one site it ran from 2.1e-08 to 1.7e-05. Estimate it from recordings of your own recorder, as the hardRain package and the authors of the method both do.

The hardRain package can also be accessed via this wrapper.

References

Bedoya C, Isaza C, Daza JM, López JD (2017). “Automatic identification of rainfall in acoustic recordings.” Ecological Indicators, 75, 95–100. doi:10.1016/j.ecolind.2016.12.018 .

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rainfallDetection(sheep, method="bedoya2017")
} # }
